output.title: Scope creep is usually a boundary problem
output.body:
If you run a one-person business, scope creep is usually not a motivation problem. It is a workflow-boundary problem: the work keeps expanding because nothing says where the task starts, where it stops, and what gets deferred.

The useful question is not, “Can I use AI somewhere?” It is, “Which one recurring task keeps pulling me away from core work?” Think customer questions, invoice data entry, or lead follow-up. If a task does not repeat often enough to describe clearly, automation is probably the wrong tool. If it does repeat and has a measurable outcome, it may be worth a bounded automation instead of another afternoon of manual work or hiring.

That is the same kind of diagnostic Bareni uses: identify the one recurring workflow, say honestly whether AI fits, and only then define a narrow pilot scope. Human approval stays in place for money movement and anything sensitive.

If you have already tried ChatGPT but have not tied it to a real workflow, start with one self-check: which task do you repeat most often that someone else could complete without changing the decision? That is usually where the boundary belongs. Sometimes the tidy answer is that the task should stay manual.】【。
